mainTopic: Doubt and danger: uncovered liquids, and a knife found notched after שחיטה (רב הונא vs. רב חסדא)
overview: This amud opens at the end of a discussion about a ברייתא on vessels whose covering changed while the owner was away. Creeping creatures uncover vessels but do not cover them, so the two cases are treated differently. If the vessel was found just as it was left, there is no טומאה at all. Exposed water, though, is forbidden even in a case of doubt, and the גמרא concludes חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא: danger is treated more strictly than a prohibition. It then quotes a משנה in תרומות: water, wine and milk become forbidden when left uncovered long enough for a snake to come out, drink, and go back to its hole. Next comes a מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב חסדא about a knife found notched after שחיטה and then used to break bones. רב חסדא rules the animal כשרה, because a ספק does not override a ודאי. רבא challenges this from a case of טבילה, and through a series of back-and-forth answers the גמרא concludes that the knife was flawed, not the animal. Finally, a ברייתא saying 'any doubt in שחיטה is invalid' is explained as covering doubts about pausing or pressing, not the notched knife.

steps.title: Creeping creatures uncover vessels but do not cover them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the בריתא treats 'found uncovered' more leniently than 'found covered.' Creeping creatures tend to uncover vessels, so the uncovering can be blamed on them rather than on an impure person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because creeping creatures usually uncover vessels, and they do not usually cover them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to a question about the בריתא. It explains why a vessel found covered is treated as טמא, while a vessel found uncovered is only treated as פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel was left uncovered and later found covered, only a person could have covered it, and that person may have been טמא. If it was left covered and later found uncovered, a creeping creature may have uncovered it to drink. So we do not assume an impure person was involved, and the contents are only disqualified, not impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Small creeping creatures, such as weasels and snakes

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an answer. The question it answers comes right before this part of the דף: why does the בריתא say 'טמא' in one case but only 'פסול' in the other?

phrases.english: Because it is the way of creeping creatures to uncover,
and it is not their way to cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a question raised just before this part of the דף, about the difference between the two halves of the בריתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the difference using a fact of nature: creeping creatures uncover vessels but never cover them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think both changes (covered to uncovered, and uncovered to covered) should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Uncovering can be blamed on a creeping creature, so the contents are only disqualified. Covering must have been done by a person, who may have been impure.

steps.title: A second inference: if nothing changed, there is no problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to read the בריתא. It only rules strictly when the vessel's state changed. If he found it exactly as he left it, there is neither טומאה nor פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the reason for the strict ruling is that he left it uncovered and found it covered, or left it covered and found it uncovered. But if he found it just as he left it, there is no impurity and no disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to draw a lenient inference from the בריתא. It is preparing for the contrast with exposed water in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict ruling depends on a change in the vessel's state. From this we learn that if nothing changed, the vessel is fine, even though there is still some doubt about what happened in the meantime. This shows that for טומאה and פסול, some cases of doubt are ruled leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: But this other case (introduces an inference from the opposite case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'found it uncovered' with 'found it as he left it.' Here the case is that he left it uncovered and found it still uncovered. For טומאה this is no problem, but the next step shows that for drinking water it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
the reason is that he left it uncovered
and came and found it covered,
or left it covered and came and found it uncovered;
but if he found it just as he left it,

phrases.aramaic: לָא טוּמְאָה אִיכָּא וְלָא פְּסוּלָא אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: there is neither impurity nor disqualification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent inference from the same בריתא that also shows leniency in a case of doubt.
steps.raayaObject: That for טומאה and disqualification, there are cases of doubt where the ruling is lenient.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בריתא's wording: it rules strictly only when the vessel's state changed, so if it is unchanged, the contents are fine.

steps.title: Danger is treated more strictly than a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Exposed water is forbidden in any case of doubt, even though doubts about טומאה can be lenient. The גמרא concludes חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא, danger is more severe than a prohibition, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet a doubt about exposed water makes it forbidden. Learn from this that danger is treated more strictly than a prohibition. Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the lenient rule for טומאה against the strict rule for exposed water. From the difference it draws a major principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טומאה and איסור there are cases of doubt where we are lenient. With exposed water, the worry is that a snake drank from it and left poison. Here any doubt makes the water forbidden, because a risk to life is taken more seriously than a ritual prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Water left uncovered, which might have been drunk from by a snake
Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from what came before)
Danger is more severe than a prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא: in matters of physical danger, we are stricter than with ordinary prohibitions. A doubt about טומאה can sometimes be ruled leniently, but a doubt about danger, such as exposed water, is ruled strictly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle in הלכה: rules meant to protect health and life are applied even more strictly than ritual prohibitions.

phrases.english: whereas, with uncertainly exposed water, it is forbidden;
phrases.notes: He left the water uncovered and found it still uncovered, yet we still worry a snake drank from it.

phrases.english: learn from it:
danger is more severe than prohibition.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ סְפֵק מַיִם מְגוּלִּים אֲסוּרִין, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the leniency shown in steps 1 and 2 as a contrast to draw a general principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Danger is treated more strictly than a prohibition: exposed water is forbidden even in a case of doubt.

steps.title: The משנה: three liquids forbidden when left uncovered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in תרומות. Water, wine and milk become forbidden when left uncovered. They must stand long enough for a snake to come out of a nearby place and drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: three liquids are forbidden because they were left uncovered: water, wine and milk. How long must they stand to become forbidden? Long enough for a snake to come out from a nearby place and drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new source, a משנה about which liquids become forbidden when uncovered and how long that takes. It is setting up a question about one of the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה gives the basic rules of גילוי: only these three liquids, and only after enough time has passed for a snake to reach them and drink. The phrase 'a nearby place' is left undefined, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature, here meaning a snake

phrases.english: We learned there, in a Mishnah:
Three liquids are forbidden because of being uncovered:
water, wine, and milk.
How long must they stand uncovered and become forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא הָרַחַשׁ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב וְיִשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.english: Enough time for the creeping creature to come out from a nearby place and drink.
phrases.notes: The 'creeping creature' here is a snake, whose poison is the danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַשְׁקִין אֲסוּרִין מִשּׁוּם גִּלּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having established that exposed liquids are dangerous, the גמרא now brings the משנה that sets out the rules of גילוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water, wine and milk become forbidden once they have stood uncovered long enough for a snake to come out from a nearby place and drink.

steps.title: How close is 'a nearby place'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define the משנה's phrase 'a nearby place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how near is 'a nearby place'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of a phrase in the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of time needed depends on how far away the snake is imagined to be. So defining 'a nearby place' tells us how quickly uncovered liquids become forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much (how far, how long)?

phrases.english: And how near is a nearby place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a phrase in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance meant by 'a nearby place,' which sets how long liquids must be uncovered before they become forbidden.

steps.title: Even from under the vessel's handle
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה answers that 'nearby' is very close. It is enough time for a snake to come out from under the vessel's own handle and drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה, said: enough time for a snake to come out from under the handle of the vessel and drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה answers the question. He defines 'a nearby place' as the space right under the vessel's handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the snake is imagined to be hiding right at the vessel, the time needed is very short. So liquids become forbidden after only a brief time uncovered, which fits the strict approach to danger.

keyTerms.meaning: The handle of a vessel (literally, the vessel's 'ear')

steps.whatToRemember: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה defines 'a nearby place' as close as right under the vessel's own handle, so only a short time is needed. Step 8 adjusts the time measure: it must also include the snake going back to its hole.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִתַּחַת אוֹזֶן כְּלִי וְיִשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.english: Enough time for it to come out from beneath the handle of the vessel and drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'A nearby place' means even right under the vessel's handle, so only a very short time is needed for the liquid to become forbidden.

steps.title: If He Watches the Snake Drink, Where Is the Doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה's time measure. If the snake only comes out from under the handle and drinks, the owner would see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only long enough to drink? But he would see it drinking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 6. If the time measure is only for the snake to come out and drink, the owner would see the snake, so there would be no doubt at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole worry about exposed liquid is that a snake might have drunk without anyone noticing. A snake drinking right next to the cup, in a very short time, would be seen. So that time measure cannot be what creates the danger.

phrases.english: It drinks? But he sees it!
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the owner of the liquid. If the snake drinks right in front of him, he would notice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the time measure given in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The measure of 'come out from under the handle and drink'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the snake drinks in that short time, the owner would see it, so there would be no hidden danger to worry about.

steps.title: Drink and Go Back to Its Hole
steps.stepSummary: The measure is the time for the snake to come out, drink, and return to its hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: long enough for it to drink and go back to its hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the measure. The liquid must stand long enough for the snake to come out, drink, and also go back into its hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the trip back to the hole makes the time long enough that the snake could come and go without the owner seeing. Now there is a real doubt about whether venom got into the liquid.
steps.whatToRemember: Exposed liquid becomes forbidden after enough time for a snake to come out of a nearby place, drink, and return to its hole unseen.

phrases.english: Rather, it drinks and returns to its hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The time is just long enough for the snake to come out and drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time is long enough for the snake to come out, drink, and return to its hole, so it could happen unseen.

steps.title: A Knife Found Notched After Slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about a knife found notched after שחיטה when it was also used afterward to break bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: someone slaughtered with a knife and it was later found notched. רב הונא says that even if he broke bones with it all day, the שחיטה is פסולה, because we worry it got notched on the hide. רב חסדא says it is כשרה, because maybe it got notched on a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב חסדא. The knife was found notched, and nobody knows whether the notch came during the שחיטה or afterward while breaking bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A notched knife makes the שחיטה פסולה if the notch was there while cutting. רב הונא worries the notch happened on the animal's hide during the שחיטה. רב חסדא says it more likely happened later on the bones, so the שחיטה stays כשרה.

phrases.english: It was stated: One who slaughters with a knife
and it was found notched,
Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שִׁיבֵּר בָּהּ עֲצָמוֹת כׇּל הַיּוֹם –
phrases.english: Even if he broke bones with it all day –
it is invalid; we are concerned that perhaps it became notched on the hide.
And Rav Chisda said: It is valid,
for perhaps it became notched on a bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, still dealing with how to handle doubts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the שחיטה is פסולה, since the notch may have come from the hide. רב חסדא: it is כשרה, since the notch may have come from the bones.

steps.title: What Is רב חסדא's Reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that רב הונא follows his known view, and asks for רב חסדא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא fits his own earlier teaching. But what is רב חסדא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it understands רב הונא, because his ruling matches a teaching of his we already know. It now asks why רב חסדא rules leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's strictness is easy to understand. A living animal is assumed forbidden until we know it was slaughtered properly, and here we are not sure. רב חסדא seems to ignore that doubt, so the גמרא wants his logic.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with his own teaching

phrases.english: Granted, Rav Huna follows his own teaching,
phrases.notes: His earlier teaching (on דף ט׳): a living animal is assumed forbidden until we know it was slaughtered properly.

phrases.english: but Rav Chisda, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב הוּנָא כִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ, אֶלָּא רַב חִסְדָּא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind one side of the מחלוקת in Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא allows the meat even though the animal started off assumed forbidden

steps.title: A Doubt Cannot Push Away a Certainty
steps.stepSummary: Bone definitely notches a knife, while hide only maybe does. A ספק cannot override a ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: bone surely notches a knife. Hide maybe notches it and maybe not. So this is a doubt against a certainty, and a doubt does not push away a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב חסדא's reason. Since bones surely cause notches and hide only maybe does, we blame the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know for sure that breaking bones notches a knife. Whether hide notches it is only a doubt. The rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי tells us to go with the sure cause, so the שחיטה is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt does not take something out of a certainty

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is a basic tool for deciding doubts all over ש״ס, and the rest of this סוגיא tests it.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'certainty' here is not that this specific notch came from bone. It means bone is a sure cause of notches in general, while hide is only a possible cause.

phrases.english: He can say to you: A bone certainly notches,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר – סָפֵק פּוֹגֵם סָפֵק לָא פּוֹגֵם,
phrases.english: hide may notch and may not notch,
so it is a case of doubt and certainty,
and a doubt does not take something out of a certainty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bone surely notches and hide only maybe does. Since a ספק cannot override a ודאי, we blame the bone.

steps.title: רבא's Challenge From Immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב חסדא, in support of רב הונא, using a ברייתא about טבילה where a doubt does override a certainty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected, to support רב הונא: someone immersed and came out, and a blocking item was found on him. Even if he handled that type of item all day, the טבילה does not count until he can say, 'I am sure it was not on me before.' Here he surely immersed, and it is only a doubt whether the item was on him then, yet the doubt overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב חסדא's rule. In the case of טבילה, a doubt about a blocking item cancels a sure immersion, even though he worked with that item all day afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case closely matches the knife: there is a likely later cause (handling the item all day), just like breaking bones. Still, the ברייתא is strict and does not credit the טבילה. That looks like a ספק overriding a ודאי, which goes against רב חסדא's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A blocking item between the body and the water

phrases.english: Rava objected, to support Rav Huna:
One immersed and came up,
and a blocking item was found on him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְעַסֵּק בְּאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין
phrases.english: even though he was busy with that same type of item
the entire day –
phrases.notes: After the טבילה. So the item could easily have stuck to him later, just as the bones could have notched the knife later.

phrases.english: the immersion does not count for him,
until he will say:

phrases.aramaic: ״בָּרִי לִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עָלַי קוֹדֶם לָכֵן״.
phrases.english: 'I am certain that it was not on me before that.'
But here, where he certainly immersed,
it is a doubt whether it was on him
or whether it was not on him,
and the doubt comes and takes it out of the certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle given in Step 11 for רב חסדא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's principle that a ספק does not override a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the טבילה case the immersion is certain and the blocking item is only a doubt, yet the ברייתא cancels the טבילה. So a ספק can override a ודאי, which supports רב הונא.

steps.title: The immersion case is different because the person was already impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. In the טבילה case, the person's earlier status of טומאה supports the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since one can say: keep the impure person in his presumed status, and say he did not immerse properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's challenge from step 12. It says the טבילה case is not a fair comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the טבילה case, the doubt is not standing alone. The person was definitely טמא before, and that חזקה joins the doubt. So the doubt plus the חזקה can override what looked certain, but that does not prove a bare ספק beats a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case being compared is not the same
Presumed status; we assume something stays as it was until proven otherwise
Keep it in its presumed status

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא about טבילה that רבא just brought.

phrases.english: since one can say:
keep the impure person in his presumed status,
and say that he did not immerse properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 12 by telling apart the טבילה case and the knife case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the טבילה ברייתא as proof against רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the טבילה case the doubt is backed by an existing חזקת טומאה, so it is not a plain ספק against a ודאי.

steps.title: The animal also has an earlier forbidden status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the animal also had a presumed status before. It was forbidden while alive, so we should say it was not properly slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, keep the animal in its presumed status, and say it was not properly slaughtered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument back on רב חסדא. If the person's old status counts, the animal's old status should count too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, an animal is forbidden to eat. That is its חזקה. If we follow the person's old status in the טבילה case, we should follow the animal's old forbidden status here and make it forbidden, like רב הונא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same reasoning should apply in this case

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the knife case, where the knife was found notched after the שחיטה.

phrases.english: keep the animal in its presumed status,
and say that it was not properly slaughtered!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, הַעֲמֵד בְּהֵמָה עַל חֶזְקָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חזקה reasoning from step 13 to the animal, which would weaken רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference drawn in step 13 between the טבילה case and the knife case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal also has an earlier status, a forbidden one, so the same reasoning should make it forbidden.

steps.title: The slaughtered animal is in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the animal's old status has already changed, because we can see an animal that was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, a slaughtered animal is in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the animal's old forbidden status does not count anymore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is no longer simply a live, forbidden animal. A שחיטה clearly took place, so its old status is already broken. We cannot just fall back on "it was never slaughtered."

keyTerms.meaning: Look, it is right in front of you

phrases.english: Look, a slaughtered animal is in front of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the old חזקה has already been broken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal's old forbidden status should decide the case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שחיטה we can see breaks the old status, so the animal's earlier forbidden status cannot be relied on.

steps.title: The person also clearly immersed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in the טבילה case too, we know the person immersed, so his old status of טומאה should be broken as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, look, he immersed in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer of step 15 against the טבילה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seeing the שחיטה breaks the animal's old status, then knowing the person immersed should break his old status of טומאה too. Then the difference drawn in step 13 would fall apart.

phrases.english: Here too,
look, he immersed in front of you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 15 back onto the טבילה case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of step 13 that the person's חזקת טומאה is still in place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טבילה that clearly happened should break his old status, just as the שחיטה did for the animal.

steps.title: A flaw was found on the person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the טבילה case a problem was actually found on the person, the thing blocking the water, so his טבילה is in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a flaw showed up on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the person's טבילה does not automatically break his old status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something blocking the water was found on the person's body. That flaw is on the person himself. So his טבילה is weakened, and his old status of טומאה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Was born in it; showed up in it

phrases.english: But a flaw showed up on him.
phrases.notes: The flaw is the blocking thing found on his body after the טבילה, from רבא's ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a real difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבילה should break the person's old status, just as the שחיטה breaks the animal's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flaw found on the person weakens his טבילה, so his old status of טומאה stands.

steps.title: The slaughter also has a flaw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the שחיטה also has a flaw, because the knife was found notched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, a flaw showed up in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that the knife case has a flaw too, so the two cases should be treated the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The notched knife casts doubt on the שחיטה, just as the blocking thing casts doubt on the טבילה. If a flaw brings back the old status for the person, it should bring back the animal's forbidden status too.

keyTerms.meaning: In it (feminine), meaning the animal or its שחיטה

phrases.english: Here too,
a flaw showed up in it!
phrases.notes: The flaw is the notch found in the knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 17 to the knife case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The notched knife is also a flaw, so the animal's old forbidden status should come back.

steps.title: The knife is flawed, not the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final answer: the flaw is in the knife, not in the animal itself, so the animal stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The knife became flawed; the animal did not become flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer and protects רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the טבילה case, the blocking thing was found on the person's own body. In the שחיטה case, the notch is only on the knife, and nothing is wrong with the animal itself. So the slaughtered animal keeps its status as permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: A flaw found on the subject itself, like a person's body, can bring back its old status. A flaw found only on an outside tool, like the knife, does not take away the status of the animal itself. This is how רב חסדא's ruling survives רבא's challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general idea: where the doubt sits matters. A flaw on the person or thing itself is stronger than a flaw on a tool used on it.

phrases.english: The knife became flawed;
the animal did not become flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 18 and closes the defense of רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tells apart where the flaw sits: on the subject itself or on an outside tool.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A notched knife is a flaw just like the blocking thing found on the person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the knife is flawed, not the animal, so the animal stays permitted and רב חסדא's view stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a windpipe found displaced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a bird whose windpipe was found displaced. Since no one knows whether it happened before or after the cutting, the חכמים ruled that any doubt in שחיטה makes it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: If he cut the gullet and afterward the windpipe was displaced, the bird is kosher. If the windpipe was displaced first and then he cut the gullet, it is invalid. If he cut the gullet and then found the windpipe displaced, and he does not know if it happened before or after, this was a real case, and the חכמים said: any doubt in שחיטה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב חסדא. This step only sets out the source; the exact attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird needs only one סימן cut, so cutting the gullet alone is enough. If the windpipe moved out of place only after that, the bird is fine. If it moved before, the bird is invalid. When we cannot tell which came first, the חכמים ruled the bird invalid and stated a broad rule: 'Any doubt in שחיטה is invalid.'

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet (food pipe), one of the two סימנים cut in שחיטה
Was displaced, slipped out of its normal place
A doubt about whether the שחיטה was done properly
This was a real case that came before the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: The windpipe case on its own does not contradict רב חסדא, because the problem there is in the animal's body. The challenge rests on the broad word 'any' (כל) in the rule.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he cut the gullet
and afterward the windpipe was displaced – it is kosher,
phrases.notes: This is a bird, and cutting just one סימן is enough for a bird.

phrases.english: if the windpipe was displaced

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּשֶׁט – פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: and afterward he cut the gullet – it is invalid.
If he cut the gullet
and the windpipe was found displaced,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and he does not know
whether it was displaced before the slaughter
or whether it was displaced after the slaughter,
this was an actual incident, and they said:
Any doubt in slaughter is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the distinction between the knife and the animal is settled, the גמרא opens a new challenge to רב חסדא from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a knife found notched after the שחיטה leaves the animal kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states a broad rule that any doubt in שחיטה invalidates it. That seems to cover a doubt about when the knife was notched.

steps.title: What does the word 'any' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the broad word 'any' adds. It suggests that it adds cases like ours, where it is unclear when the knife became notched.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Any doubt in שחיטה': what does it come to include? Does it not come to include a case like this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes the challenge clear. It argues that the word 'any' must be adding our case of the notched knife, which would go against רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have simply ruled on the windpipe case. Adding 'any' suggests a wider rule. The most natural extra case seems to be a doubt like ours, where it is unclear whether the knife was notched before or after the cutting.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include? (asking what an extra word adds)

phrases.english: 'Any doubt in slaughter' –
what does it come to include?
Does it not come to include a case like this one?
phrases.notes: 'This one' means our case: the knife was found notched, and we don't know if that happened before or after the cutting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא from the previous step and points out the word that threatens רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling about the notched knife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word 'any' should add something, and the obvious addition is a doubt about the knife. That would make the animal invalid, against רב חסדא.

steps.title: 'Any' adds doubts about pausing or pressing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'any' adds other doubts: whether the slaughterer paused in the middle, or whether he pressed the knife down. It does not add the notched knife case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to include a doubt whether he paused and a doubt whether he pressed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It says the word 'any' adds different cases, not the notched knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pausing in the middle (שהיה) and pressing the knife down (דרסה) are mistakes in the cutting itself, and either one makes a שחיטה invalid. 'Any' teaches that even a doubt about these makes it invalid. Since the word has these cases to add, it does not need to cover the knife doubt, so רב חסדא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He paused in the middle of the שחיטה (שְׁהִיָּה), which makes it invalid
He pressed the knife down instead of drawing it across (דְּרָסָה), which makes it invalid

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rule 'any doubt in שחיטה is invalid' covers doubts about how the cutting was done, such as pausing or pressing. It does not cover רב חסדא's case of a knife found notched afterward.

phrases.english: No, it comes to include
a doubt whether he paused, a doubt whether he pressed.
phrases.notes: These are two of the classic mistakes that ruin a שחיטה: stopping in the middle, or pushing the knife down instead of drawing it across.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי סָפֵק שָׁהָה, סָפֵק דָּרַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by giving 'any' a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the extra word: it adds other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Any doubt' includes a doubt about when the knife was notched, which would go against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Any doubt' includes doubts about pausing or pressing during the cutting, so רב חסדא's ruling is not contradicted.
